verdict.rationale: The docs say Solo builds with a default attestation key and that you can generate, sign and program your own attestation key pair across many devices. That gives a relying party something to verify at enrollment, and a custom key could be used to recognize only approved devices. However, these docs come from the customization and building pages tied to the STM32L432 (Solo 1) firmware path, not clearly to Solo 2, and nothing describes how a verifier would check the attestation. Missing for 10: Solo 2-specific attestation certificate/AAGUID documentation, FIDO Metadata Service listing or published root certificates for relying-party verification, guidance on enforcing approved models at registration, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
